The Prophet overpowered a jinn demon that tried to interrupt his prayer, but did not tie it to a mosque pillar, remembering Solomon's prayer for a unique kingdom.
When devils were barred from the news of heaven, jinn heard the Prophet reciting in Fajr at Nakhla, believed, and Allah revealed Surat al-Jinn about them.
A tree told the Prophet of the jinn who heard the Quran; he tells Abu Huraira not to bring bones or dung for cleaning, as they are the jinn's food.
Ibn Masud said the verse on those called upon who seek access to their Lord concerns jinn worshipped by some people, who became Muslims while their worshippers kept their religion.
A jinn demon tried to disturb the Prophet's prayer; he overpowered it and meant to tie it to a pillar, but released it recalling Solomon's prayer for a unique kingdom.
Barred from heaven's news by flames, devils search the world and some hear the Prophet reciting at the Fajr prayer, believe, tell their people, and Surat al-Jinn is revealed.
Soothsayers are nothing; the one true word they tell is snatched from heaven by a jinn and poured into their ears, and they mix it with a hundred lies.
